newsitem.title: USA: Time Warner re-evaluating U S West - WSJ.
newsitem.headline: Time Warner re-evaluating U S West - WSJ.

text.p: Time Warner Inc, buoyed by the surging value for cable-TV systems, is reconsidering its plan to restructure its partnership with U S West, the Wall Street Journal said.
In Wednesday's electronic edition, the Journal said that Time Warner Vice Chairman Ted Turner has told some people in recent weeks that the restructuring will no longer take place.
Time Warner has been trying to renegotiate a restructuring of the partnership for more than two years.

However, Turner has told people in the financial community that the two companies are far apart in setting a breakup value and that the climbing value of cable properties makes it a bad time to part with the assets.
People close to the talks said the two companies remain $1 billion apart in negotiations over a breakup.

Unnamed sources close to Time Warner said a deal with U S West is still possible, and that the company is still seeking to lighten its exposure to cable and to reduce debt by selling or spinning off businesses with some of the several million cable subscribers it owns outside of the partnership.

Time Warner said that "the talks are ongoing, but there is a value gap." A spokesman for U S West Media, which controls 25.5 percent of Time Warner Entertainment, told the Journal: "We continue to have discussions. We do not feel a burning need to restructure."
The partnership, with estimated assets of more than $20 billion, controls the Warner Bros. film studio, the Home Box Office pay-television and 9.8 million cable subscribers.
